lessons.title: Quarter Notes
lessons.description: Play one alternating stroke on every beat.
tips: Count aloud with each click.
Match the sound of both hands.
Keep the sticks relaxed between beats.

lessons.title: Eighth Notes
lessons.description: Play two alternating strokes per beat.
tips: Count one and, two and.
Keep the notes equally spaced.
Listen for an even sound from both hands.

lessons.title: Triplet Notes
lessons.description: Play three alternating strokes per beat.
tips: Count one trip let for each beat.
Keep all three notes evenly spaced.
Notice that the leading hand changes each beat.

lessons.title: Sixteenth Notes
lessons.description: Play four alternating strokes per beat.
tips: Count one e and a.
Stay loose as the notes get closer.
Keep each beat aligned with the click.

lessons.title: Changing Subdivisions
lessons.description: Move from one to two, three, then four alternating strokes per beat.
tips: Keep the beat steady as the subdivision changes.
Count each new group before playing.
Continue alternating hands through each change.

lessons.title: Single Stroke Roll
lessons.description: Sixteenth notes, one stroke per hand in turn: R L R L. The foundation of every roll and most fills.
tips: Start each stroke from the same height so both hands sound alike.
Let the stick bounce back up on its own; lift, don't press.
Speed comes last: keep it even at a slow tempo before raising it.

lessons.title: Single Stroke Four
lessons.description: A 4-stroke phrase of alternating single strokes, ending with an accent and a rest.
tips: Begin slowly and keep the strokes evenly spaced.
Use relaxed hands and match the sound of both sticks.
Keep the pulse steady through the rests before repeating.

lessons.title: Single Stroke Seven
lessons.description: A 7-stroke phrase of alternating single strokes, ending with an accent and a rest.
tips: Begin slowly and keep the strokes evenly spaced.
Use relaxed hands and match the sound of both sticks.
Keep the pulse steady through the rests before repeating.

lessons.title: Multiple Bounce Roll
lessons.description: A buzz roll: each hand presses the stick into the head so it bounces several times, and the hands alternate on every eighth note.
tips: Keep a little pressure in the fingers so each stroke buzzes rather than bounces twice.
Aim for one smooth, continuous sound with no gaps where the hands change.
Keep both hands' buzzes the same length and volume.

lessons.title: Triple Stroke Roll
lessons.description: Groups of three strokes per hand, alternating right and left, with a short rest between groups.
tips: Begin slowly and keep the strokes evenly spaced.
Use relaxed hands and match the sound of both sticks.
Keep the pulse steady through the rests before repeating.

lessons.title: Double Stroke Open Roll
lessons.description: Two strokes per hand, R R L L. Each slashed eighth note is played as two sixteenths with the same hand.
tips: Make the second stroke of each pair as loud as the first.
At slow tempos play both strokes from the wrist; let the fingers take over as it speeds up.
Listen for a steady stream of notes, not pairs.

lessons.title: Five Stroke Roll
lessons.description: A 5-stroke phrase built from same-hand pairs and a closing stroke, ending with an accent and a rest.
tips: Begin slowly and keep the strokes evenly spaced.
Use relaxed hands and match the sound of both sticks.
Keep the pulse steady through the rests before repeating.

lessons.title: Six Stroke Roll
lessons.description: A 6-stroke phrase built from same-hand pairs and a closing stroke, ending with an accent and a rest.
tips: Begin slowly and keep the strokes evenly spaced.
Use relaxed hands and match the sound of both sticks.
Keep the pulse steady through the rests before repeating.

lessons.title: Seven Stroke Roll
lessons.description: A 7-stroke phrase built from same-hand pairs and a closing stroke, ending with an accent and a rest.
tips: Begin slowly and keep the strokes evenly spaced.
Use relaxed hands and match the sound of both sticks.
Keep the pulse steady through the rests before repeating.

lessons.title: Nine Stroke Roll
lessons.description: A 9-stroke phrase built from same-hand pairs and a closing stroke, ending with an accent and a rest.
tips: Begin slowly and keep the strokes evenly spaced.
Use relaxed hands and match the sound of both sticks.
Keep the pulse steady through the rests before repeating.

lessons.title: Ten Stroke Roll
lessons.description: A 10-stroke phrase built from same-hand pairs and a closing stroke, ending with an accent and a rest.
tips: Begin slowly and keep the strokes evenly spaced.
Use relaxed hands and match the sound of both sticks.
Keep the pulse steady through the rests before repeating.

lessons.title: Eleven Stroke Roll
lessons.description: A 11-stroke phrase built from same-hand pairs and a closing stroke, ending with an accent and a rest.
tips: Begin slowly and keep the strokes evenly spaced.
Use relaxed hands and match the sound of both sticks.
Keep the pulse steady through the rests before repeating.

lessons.title: Thirteen Stroke Roll
lessons.description: A 13-stroke phrase built from same-hand pairs and a closing stroke, ending with an accent and a rest.
tips: Begin slowly and keep the strokes evenly spaced.
Use relaxed hands and match the sound of both sticks.
Keep the pulse steady through the rests before repeating.

lessons.title: Fifteen Stroke Roll
lessons.description: A 15-stroke phrase built from same-hand pairs and a closing stroke, ending with an accent and a rest.
tips: Begin slowly and keep the strokes evenly spaced.
Use relaxed hands and match the sound of both sticks.
Keep the pulse steady through the rests before repeating.

lessons.title: Seventeen Stroke Roll
lessons.description: A 17-stroke phrase built from same-hand pairs and a closing stroke, ending with an accent and a rest.
tips: Begin slowly and keep the strokes evenly spaced.
Use relaxed hands and match the sound of both sticks.
Keep the pulse steady through the rests before repeating.

lessons.title: Single Paradiddle
lessons.description: Two single strokes and a double, R L R R, then the same starting on the left, L R L L. The first note of each group is accented.
tips: Play the accent from a higher stick and the other notes low.
The double at the end of each group sets up the other hand's accent; keep it relaxed.
Say it as you play: pa-ra-did-dle.

lessons.title: Double Paradiddle
lessons.description: Four alternating singles lead into a double. Each six-note group changes the lead hand.
tips: Count six even notes in each group.
Let the final double prepare the next lead hand.
Keep the accents clear without tightening your grip.

lessons.title: Triple Paradiddle
lessons.description: Six alternating singles lead into a double, then the pattern starts with the other hand.
tips: Count eight even strokes per group.
Keep the last two strokes of each group even.
Bring out the first note without speeding up.

lessons.title: Single Paradiddle-Diddle
lessons.description: Two alternating singles followed by two doubles, written here as sixteenth-note sextuplets.
tips: Say the six hands slowly before playing.
Listen for two balanced strokes in each double.
Use lead-with-left to practice the mirrored sticking.

lessons.title: Flam
lessons.description: A quiet grace note just before an accented main note, alternating hands: the grace note is played by the other hand.
tips: Hold the grace-note stick low and the main stick high, so both land almost together.
Aim for one thick sound, not two separate hits.
After each flam, the hand that played the main note drops low for the next grace note.

lessons.title: Flam Accent
lessons.description: Triplets with an accented flam on the first note of each beat, followed by two quiet taps. The lead hand changes every beat.
tips: Count it in threes: flam, tap, tap.
Keep the two taps low and even, so the accented flam stands out.
The last tap of each group is the next flam's grace note hand; let it stay low.

lessons.title: Flam Tap
lessons.description: Alternating same-hand doubles with a flam on the first stroke, played as continuous triplets.
tips: Keep the grace note low.
Match the spacing from flam to tap on each hand.
Count the triplets while the two-stroke groups move across the beat.

lessons.title: Flamacue
lessons.description: Five alternating main strokes framed by flams, with the accent on the second stroke.
tips: Play the second note louder than its neighbors.
Keep the framing flams soft and close.
Hear the closing flam before starting the other hand.

lessons.title: Flam Paradiddle
lessons.description: A paradiddle with a flam on the first stroke of each group.
tips: Play the underlying paradiddle evenly.
Keep the grace stroke close to the accented main note.
Let the final double set up the opposite lead.

lessons.title: Single Flammed Mill
lessons.description: An inverted paradiddle beginning with a flam and a same-hand tap.
tips: Practice the four main strokes without the grace first.
Keep the tap after the flam low.
Listen for a smooth change to the other hand.

lessons.title: Flam Paradiddle-Diddle
lessons.description: A paradiddle-diddle with a flam at the start, written as sixteenth-note sextuplets.
tips: Keep the six main strokes evenly spaced.
Separate the soft grace stroke from the following doubles.
Switch the lead hand using the practice control.

lessons.title: Pataflafla
lessons.description: Four alternating strokes with flams on the first and fourth.
tips: Count the two quiet middle taps.
Make both flams clear without widening them.
Notice the adjacent flams across each group boundary.

lessons.title: Swiss Army Triplet
lessons.description: A flam, a same-hand tap and an opposite-hand tap make one triplet.
tips: Count each three-note group evenly.
Keep the tap after the flam quiet.
Use lead-with-left to mirror the exercise.

lessons.title: Inverted Flam Tap
lessons.description: Continuous triplets with a flam followed by the opposite hand; the next flam completes that hand's double.
tips: Listen for the double that crosses the group boundary.
Play the first flam gently until the sticking feels natural.
Count the triplets as the two-stroke groups move across the beat.

lessons.title: Flam Drag
lessons.description: Triplets alternate a flam, a dragged note and a tap; each new group changes hands.
tips: Keep the two drag grace notes low and close.
Keep the three main notes evenly spaced.
Practice each hand slowly before raising the tempo.

lessons.title: Drag
lessons.description: Two quick grace notes from one hand, played as a soft double stroke, lead into an accented note from the other hand.
tips: Play the two grace notes low and close together, like a small bounce.
Keep them quieter than the main note, which is accented.
Practice the grace notes alone first: a soft, even double stroke.

lessons.title: Single Drag Tap
lessons.description: Offset doubles place a drag and accent on the second stroke of each pair.
tips: Keep each grace-note double low.
Listen for the doubles crossing the beat.
Match the accents on both hands.

lessons.title: Double Drag Tap
lessons.description: Two dragged notes lead into an accented tap in each triplet.
tips: Practice both drags slowly.
Keep the final accent in time.
Give both grace doubles the same sound.

lessons.title: Lesson 25
lessons.description: In 2/4, a drag and tap lead into an accented note.
tips: Count the short notes before the accent.
Keep the two grace notes quiet.
Try the mirrored lead with the practice control.

lessons.title: Single Dragadiddle
lessons.description: A dragged first stroke leads into a paradiddle.
tips: Play the paradiddle alone first.
Keep the grace notes softer than the main note.
Let the double set up the other hand.

lessons.title: Drag Paradiddle 1
lessons.description: An accented stroke is followed by a dragged paradiddle.
tips: Separate the opening accent from the drag.
Keep the paradiddle even.
Practice both leads at a comfortable pace.

lessons.title: Drag Paradiddle 2
lessons.description: An accented stroke and an extra drag lead into a dragged paradiddle.
tips: Keep the two drags light.
Count the change from eighths to sixteenths.
Keep the final double even.

lessons.title: Single Ratamacue
lessons.description: A dragged triplet leads to a closing accent.
tips: Count the three triplet notes evenly.
Save the strongest stroke for the end.
Make the grace double quiet and clear.

lessons.title: Double Ratamacue
lessons.description: An extra dragged note leads into the triplet and closing accent.
tips: Keep both drags light.
Count the triplet after the first drag.
Land the final accent without rushing.

lessons.title: Triple Ratamacue
lessons.description: Three dragged notes lead into the ratamacue and its closing accent.
tips: Practice the three drags slowly.
Keep the triplet clear after the lead-in.
Save the accent for the final note.
